t: which word is spelled correctly? necessary neccessary necesary neccesary necessary has one c and two s's: ne-c-e-ss-ary. the other choices double the wrong letter or drop one s.

choose the correct spelling to complete the sentence. the patient reported three days of ______ and was given fluids to prevent dehydration. diarhea diarrhea diarrea diarreah the correct spelling is d-i-a-r-r-h-e-a: double r, then h, then e-a. it comes from greek roots meaning "flowing through," and the -rrh- pattern also shows up in hemorrhage .

which sentence is spelled correctly? the nurse will recommend a follow-up visit in two weeks. the nurse will reccomend a follow-up visit in two weeks. the nurse will recomend a follow-up visit in two weeks. the nurse will reccommend a follow-up visit in two weeks. recommend = re + commend: one c, two m's. the common mistake is doubling the c instead of the m.

choose the correct spelling of the word that means heavy, uncontrolled bleeding. hemorrhage hemorrage hemmorhage hemorhage the correct spelling is h-e-m-o-r-r-h-a-g-e: one m, double r, then h. hemo- means blood, and -rrhage means bursting forth.

the sentence below contains one misspelled word. type the word spelled correctly. the nurse kept the two patients' charts in seperate folders. the misspelled word is seperate ; the correct spelling is separate . listen for "a rat" in sep-a-rat-e.

which word in the sentence is spelled incorrectly? the clinic will immediately report any occurence of measles, and it will definitely update the vaccine schedule . immediately definitely schedule occurence occurrence needs a double c and a double r: o-c-c-u-r-r-e-n-c-e. immediately , definitely and schedule are all spelled correctly in the sentence.

which word is spelled correctly? priviledge privilege privelege privilage privilege is p-r-i-v-i-l-e-g-e. there is no d, the second vowel is i, and it ends in -ege. "priviledge" is the most common error; people add a d because of words like knowledge .

what is the correct plural of diagnosis ? diagnosises diagnosis's diagnosies diagnoses words from greek that end in -is form the plural by changing -is to -es: diagnosis → diagnoses. an apostrophe never makes a word plural, so "diagnosis's" is wrong.

a single bone of the spine is a vertebra . what is the plural? vertebraes vertebrais vertebrae vertebrea latin words that end in -a often form the plural with -ae: vertebra → vertebrae. adding another -s ("vertebraes") makes a double plural.

which sentence uses the singular and plural forms correctly? a single bacteria can divide about every 20 minutes. a single bacterium can divide about every 20 minutes. the bacterias divided about every 20 minutes. two bacterium were seen under the microscope. bacterium is singular (one cell); bacteria is plural (more than one). "a single bacteria" uses a plural word for one thing, and "bacterias" is a double plural.

which sentence is correct in standard written english? the admission criterias are listed on the program website. the admission criteria are listed on the program website. one admission criteria is a c or better in chemistry. the admission criterion are listed on the program website. criterion is singular; criteria is plural, so it takes the plural verb are . "criterias" is a double plural, "one ... criteria" uses a plural for one item, and "criterion are" pairs a singular noun with a plural verb.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the students left ______ backpacks in the chemistry lab. there they're thier their their shows ownership (the backpacks belong to the students). there is a place, they're means "they are," and "thier" is a misspelling.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. ______ going to draw blood after lunch, so the patient should keep drinking water. they're their there theyre test it: "they are going to draw blood" makes sense, so the contraction they're is correct. a contraction needs an apostrophe where letters are left out, so "theyre" is wrong.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. dehydration can ______ a patient's blood pressure. effect affect effected affects after a helping verb like can , you need the base form of a verb. affect is the verb meaning "to influence." effect is usually a noun (a result), and can affects is not grammatical.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the new medication had a calming ______ on the patient. affect affection effect effecting after the article a and an adjective ( calming ), you need a noun meaning "result," which is effect . affect here would be the verb; affection means fondness.

which sentence uses affect or effect correctly? the medicine's side affects included dizziness. cold weather can effect how quickly a wound heals. lack of sleep had a negative affect on her test score. the heat wave will affect the almond harvest schedule. the heat wave will influence the schedule, so the verb affect is correct. "side effects" and "a negative effect" are nouns, so they need effect ; "can affect how quickly" needs the verb affect .

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the ______ reason for the delay was a staffing shortage. principle principals principal principle's principal as an adjective means "main" or "most important." principle is a noun meaning a rule or belief, so it cannot describe the word reason .

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the nursing program is built on the ______ that every patient deserves respect. principal principles' principle principality here the word means a basic belief or rule, so principle is correct. principal means main or the head of a school, which does not fit.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the patient paid the nurse a ______ on her gentle technique. compliment complement complimant complament a compliment (with an i) is praise. "i like to get compliments." a complement (with an e) is something that completes or goes well with something else.

which sentences use the homophone in bold correctly? select all that apply. the red salsa is a nice complement to the grilled chicken. their going to drive to visalia this weekend. please put the gloves over there by the sink. the principle of the high school spoke at graduation. too many patients arrived at once, so the clinic opened a second room. correct: complement (goes well with), there (a place) and too (meaning "excessively"). incorrect: "their going" should be they're (they are), and the head of a school is the principal .

which words are spelled correctly? select all that apply. maintenance definately conscience embarass occasion correct: maintenance , conscience , occasion . "definately" should be definitely (it contains the word finite ), and "embarass" should be embarrass (double r and double s).

the sentence below contains one misspelled word. type the word spelled correctly. the front desk will acommodate patients who need wheelchair access. the misspelled word is acommodate ; the correct spelling is accommodate . it has a double c and a double m: a-c-c-o-m-m-o-d-a-t-e.

which sentence is punctuated correctly? bring your id your insurance card, and a list of your medications. bring, your id, your insurance card, and a list of your medications. bring your id, your insurance card, and, a list of your medications. bring your id, your insurance card, and a list of your medications. items in a series are separated by commas: id, insurance card, and list. do not put a comma between a verb and its object ("bring, your id") or right after and .

which sentence is punctuated correctly? after the storm passed, the clinic reopened. after, the storm passed the clinic reopened. after the storm, passed the clinic reopened. after the storm passed the clinic, reopened. "after the storm passed" is an introductory clause, so the comma goes after it, before the main clause. the other choices split the clause in the wrong place or separate the subject ( clinic ) from its verb ( reopened ).

lena has only one sister. which sentence is punctuated correctly? my sister who works at the county hospital, is a respiratory therapist. my sister, who works at the county hospital, is a respiratory therapist. my sister, who works at the county hospital is a respiratory therapist. my sister who works, at the county hospital is a respiratory therapist. because lena has only one sister, "who works at the county hospital" is extra (nonessential) information. nonessential clauses need a comma on both sides. using only one comma separates the subject from its verb.

which sentence is punctuated correctly? the patient felt dizzy so, the nurse helped her sit down. the patient, felt dizzy so the nurse helped her sit down. the patient felt dizzy, so the nurse helped her sit down. the patient felt, dizzy, so the nurse helped her sit down. this is a compound sentence: two independent clauses joined by the coordinating conjunction so . the comma goes before the conjunction, not after it.

which sentence uses a semicolon correctly? because the lab closes at noon; please submit samples early. the lab closes at noon; please submit samples early. the lab closes; at noon on fridays. please bring; a pen, a notebook, and goggles. a semicolon joins two complete sentences (independent clauses) that are closely related. "because the lab closes at noon" and "at noon on fridays" cannot stand alone, and a semicolon should not introduce a list.

which sentence is punctuated correctly? the road was closed, however the ambulance found another route. the road was closed however; the ambulance found another route. the road was; closed however, the ambulance found another route. the road was closed; however, the ambulance found another route. when a conjunctive adverb such as however joins two independent clauses, use a semicolon before it and a comma after it. using only a comma before however creates a comma splice.

which sentence uses a colon correctly? pack three items for clinicals: a stethoscope, a watch, and closed-toe shoes. pack: three items for clinicals, a stethoscope, a watch, and closed-toe shoes. the three items for clinicals are: a stethoscope, a watch, and closed-toe shoes. pack three items for clinicals; a stethoscope, a watch, and closed-toe shoes. a colon introduces a list when it follows a complete sentence ("pack three items for clinicals"). do not put a colon directly after a verb such as are , and do not use a semicolon to introduce a list.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. ms. vang is the only patient in room 4. the ______ chart was updated at noon. patients patient's patients' patient,s one patient owns the chart, so use the singular possessive: patient + 's. patients is a plain plural, and patients' is plural possessive (more than one patient).

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. all three ______ lockers are in the hallway. nurse's nurses nurses' nurses's there are three nurses (plural), and the lockers belong to them (possessive). for a plural noun that already ends in -s, add only an apostrophe: nurses'.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the clinic changed ______ hours for the summer. it's its' its it is its (no apostrophe) is the possessive form, like his or hers . it's always means "it is" or "it has." "its'" is never correct.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the ______ waiting room has new books and toys. childrens' children's childrens children' children is already plural and does not end in -s, so add 's: children's. "childrens" is not a word, so "childrens'" is wrong too.

which sentence uses apostrophes correctly? the garcia's moved to merced last year. the garcias' moved to merced last year. the garcias moved to merced's last year. the garcias moved to merced last year. to make a family name plural, just add -s (or -es): the garcias. an apostrophe shows possession, and nothing is owned in this sentence.

which sentence is punctuated correctly? “please take a deep breath”, the nurse said. “please take a deep breath,” the nurse said”. please take a deep breath,” the nurse said. “please take a deep breath,” the nurse said. in american english, commas and periods go inside the closing quotation mark. quotation marks come in pairs and surround only the spoken words.

which sentence is punctuated correctly? the patient asked, “when can i go home?” the patient asked, “when can i go home”? the patient asked “when can i go home?”. the patient asked, when can i go home?” the quoted words are the question, so the question mark goes inside the quotation marks. do not add a period after the closing quotation mark, and do not forget the opening quotation mark.

choose the correctly punctuated phrase. the pediatrician examined a ______ child with an ear infection. five-year-old five year old five-year old five year-old when several words work together as one adjective before a noun, connect all of them with hyphens. "five-year-old" describes the child as a single unit.

which sentence uses hyphens correctly? the clinic hired a highly-skilled pharmacist. the clinic hired a pharmacist with twenty-years of experience. the clinic hired a full-time pharmacist. the clinic hired a part time-pharmacist. full-time is a compound adjective before the noun pharmacist , so it is hyphenated. do not hyphenate after an -ly adverb (highly skilled). "twenty years" is not before a noun here, and "part time-pharmacist" puts the hyphen in the wrong place.

which sentences are punctuated correctly? select all that apply. before you eat, wash your hands. the nurse checked the patient's pulse, and she recorded it in the chart. the doctor, ordered a chest x-ray. valley fever is caused by a fungus; the fungus lives in soil. its time for the patient's medication. correct: an introductory clause with a comma, a compound sentence with a comma before and , and two related independent clauses joined by a semicolon. incorrect: never put a comma between a subject and its verb ("the doctor, ordered"), and "its time" needs it's (it is).

which sentences use apostrophes correctly? select all that apply. the doctors' lounge is on the second floor. the clinic is open monday's through friday's. james's prescription is ready at the counter. the bird hurt it's wing. the women's locker room was cleaned. correct: doctors' (lounge for many doctors), james's (singular possessive) and women's (irregular plural + 's). incorrect: days of the week are plain plurals (mondays), and the possessive of it is its .

which sentence is punctuated correctly? the clinic opened on june 3 2024, in visalia california. the clinic opened on june, 3, 2024 in visalia, california. the clinic opened on june 3, 2024, in visalia, california. the clinic opened on june 3, 2024 in, visalia california. put a comma between the day and the year, and another after the year when the sentence continues. put a comma between a city and its state.

which sentence uses end punctuation correctly? did the patient eat breakfast? the nurse asked whether the patient ate breakfast? did the patient eat breakfast. did the patient eat breakfast?. a direct question ends with a question mark. "the nurse asked whether ..." is an indirect question (a statement), so it ends with a period. never use two end marks.

which sentence is punctuated correctly? maria please, take the patient's temperature. maria please take, the patient's temperature. maria, please take the patient's, temperature. maria, please take the patient's temperature. when you speak directly to someone by name (direct address), set the name off with a comma. do not put commas between a verb and its object.

which sentence is punctuated correctly? pack healthy snacks such as: almonds, raisins, or crackers. pack healthy snacks such as almonds, raisins, or crackers. pack healthy snacks, such as, almonds, raisins, or crackers. pack healthy snacks such as almonds raisins, or crackers. do not use a colon after such as , including or for example ; the list flows right into the sentence. items in the list still need commas between them.

choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence. the list of medications ______ on the counter. are were be is the subject is list (singular). "of medications" is a prepositional phrase and does not change the subject. a singular subject takes a singular verb: is .

choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence. each of the nursing students ______ a stethoscope. have own has were given each is singular, so it takes a singular verb: has . "of the nursing students" is a prepositional phrase; it does not make the subject plural.

choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence. everyone in the waiting room ______ been called back. have has are were indefinite pronouns ending in -one, -body or -thing (everyone, somebody, nothing) are singular. a singular subject takes has .

choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence. a number of patients ______ waiting to be seen. are is was has been a number of means "several" or "many," so it takes a plural verb. compare: the number of patients is growing. (that refers to one number.)

which sentence is correct? the number of flu cases have increased this week. a number of flu cases has been reported this week. the number of flu cases has increased this week. a number of flu case have been reported this week. the number refers to a single total, so it takes the singular verb has . a number of means "many," so it would need have , and case must be plural after it.

in formal scientific writing, data is traditionally treated as a plural noun (the singular is datum ). which sentence follows this traditional rule? the data show a strong link between sleep and test scores. the data shows a strong link between sleep and test scores. the datas show a strong link between sleep and test scores. the data has showed a strong link between sleep and test scores. treated as a plural, data takes the plural verb show . "datas" is a double plural, and the past participle of show is shown , not showed .

choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence. neither the doctor nor the nurses ______ available right now. is was are has been with neither ... nor or either ... or , the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. nurses is closest and plural, so use are .

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the nurses finished ______ shift at 7 p.m. her its their they're the antecedent nurses is plural, so the pronoun must be plural: their . they're means "they are," which does not fit.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the instructor gave the lab manual to ana and ______. i myself mine me after a preposition ( to ), use the object pronoun me . test it by removing "ana and": "gave the lab manual to me," not "to i."

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. jamal and ______ will present the case study on friday. me myself mine i the pronoun is part of the subject, so use the subject pronoun i . test it: "i will present," not "me will present." myself is used only when the subject already appears in the sentence.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. to ______ should i send the referral? who whom whose who's the pronoun is the object of the preposition to , so use the object form whom . answer the question with him/her: "send it to him ." him → whom.

which sentences have correct subject–verb agreement? select all that apply. the bag of almonds is on the shelf. each of the patients have a wristband. measles is a contagious disease. the nurses on the night shift work twelve-hour shifts. there is two pharmacies on blackstone avenue. correct: bag ... is , measles is (a disease name that ends in -s but is singular) and nurses ... work . incorrect: each is singular (each ... has), and in "there is/are" sentences the subject comes after the verb (two pharmacies → are ).

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. between you and ______, the exam was easier than i expected. me i myself we between is a preposition, so it takes object pronouns: between you and me . "between you and i" is a common error that sounds formal but is incorrect.

choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence. yesterday the patient ______ a fever, so the nurse gave her acetaminophen. has had will have is having yesterday and the past-tense verb gave show that the action happened in the past. keep the tense consistent: had .

which sentence keeps verb tense consistent? she walks into the clinic and asked for a flu shot. she walked into the clinic and asks for a flu shot. she walked into the clinic and asked for a flu shot. she will walk into the clinic and asked for a flu shot. both actions happened at the same time, so both verbs should be in the same tense: walked and asked . the other choices switch between present, past or future in the middle of the sentence.

choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence. the patient has ______ two glasses of water since breakfast. drank drinked drunken drunk after has or have , use the past participle. for drink : drink, drank, (have) drunk. drank is simple past (i drank), "drinked" is not a word, and drunken is an adjective.

choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence. after surgery, the doctor told him to ______ down for an hour. lay lie laid lain lie means to recline and does not take an object. lay means to put something down and needs an object (lay the tray down). he is reclining himself, so use lie . after to , use the base form.

choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence. yesterday, the patient ______ in the waiting room for two hours. sat set sit sitted sit (to be seated) has the past tense sat . set means to place an object. yesterday calls for the past tense, so sit is wrong, and "sitted" is not a word.

which sentence avoids a dangling modifier? walking into the clinic, the long line surprised rosa. walking into the clinic, rosa noticed the long line. walking into the clinic, the line was long. walking into the clinic, there was a long line for rosa. an opening phrase like "walking into the clinic" must be followed right away by the person or thing doing the walking. only the first choice puts rosa right after the phrase; in the others, the line seems to be walking.

which sentence places the modifier correctly? the pharmacist handed the man a pill bottle labeled with his name. labeled with his name, the pharmacist handed the man a pill bottle. the pharmacist, labeled with his name, handed the man a pill bottle. the pharmacist handed the man labeled with his name a pill bottle. the bottle is what is labeled, so "labeled with his name" should sit right next to pill bottle . in the other choices, the pharmacist or the man appears to be labeled.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the new nurse speaks ______ to anxious patients. calm calmer calmness calmly the word describes how she speaks (a verb), so it must be an adverb: calmly . calm and calmer are adjectives, and calmness is a noun.

which sentences use adjectives and adverbs correctly? select all that apply. the patient feels bad about missing his appointment. she did good on the dosage calculation test. after the surgery, he is doing well. the medicine works real fast. the soup smells delicious. linking verbs (feel, smell, seem, be) are followed by adjectives: feels bad , smells delicious . well is correct for health or for how something is done. "did good" should be did well (adverb for an action), and "real fast" should be really fast .

what type of sentence is this? the nurse checked the patient's blood pressure and pulse. simple compound complex compound-complex there is one subject ( nurse ) and one verb ( checked ) in a single independent clause. "blood pressure and pulse" is a compound object, not a second clause, so the sentence is simple.

what type of sentence is this? the clinic opened at 8 a.m., and the line had formed by 7:30. simple compound complex compound-complex there are two independent clauses ("the clinic opened at 8 a.m." and "the line had formed by 7:30"). they are joined with a comma and and , and there is no dependent clause, so the sentence is compound.

what type of sentence is this? because the heat index reached 108 °f, the farm crew stopped work early. simple compound complex compound-complex "because the heat index reached 108 °f" is a dependent clause; it starts with the subordinating conjunction because . "the farm crew stopped work early" is one independent clause. one independent + at least one dependent clause = complex.

what type of sentence is this? when the ambulance arrived, the paramedics checked her airway, and the nurse called her family. simple compound complex compound-complex "when the ambulance arrived" is a dependent clause. "the paramedics checked her airway" and "the nurse called her family" are two independent clauses joined by and . two independent clauses + a dependent clause = compound-complex.

what type of sentence is this? maria and her brother studied for the teas and took practice tests every weekend. simple compound complex compound-complex there is one compound subject ( maria and her brother ) and one compound verb ( studied ... and took ). because it is still only one clause, it is a simple sentence. a compound sentence needs two complete clauses, each with its own subject.

what type of sentence is this? the student who scored highest on the teas received a scholarship. simple compound complex compound-complex "who scored highest on the teas" is a dependent (relative) clause describing student . the main clause is "the student received a scholarship." one independent + one dependent clause = complex.

which of the following is a sentence fragment? because the patient was allergic to penicillin. the patient was allergic to penicillin. stop. the doctor chose a different antibiotic. a fragment is a group of words that cannot stand alone. "because ..." begins a dependent clause and leaves the reader waiting for the main idea. "stop." is complete: it is a command with the understood subject you .

which of the following is a sentence fragment? she was running late for her shift at the hospital. running is good exercise for nurses. her shift at the hospital started at seven. running late for her shift at the hospital. "running late for her shift at the hospital" has no subject and no complete verb, so it is a fragment. in "running is good exercise," running is the subject and is is the verb, so it is complete.

which sentence is a comma splice? the patient was thirsty, so the nurse brought water. the patient was thirsty, the nurse brought water. because the patient was thirsty, the nurse brought water. the patient was thirsty; the nurse brought water. a comma splice joins two independent clauses with only a comma. fix it with a comma + fanboys conjunction, a semicolon, or a subordinating conjunction, as the other three choices do.

which revision correctly fixes this run-on sentence? the lab results came back normal the patient went home. the lab results came back normal, the patient went home. the lab results came back normal so, the patient went home. the lab results came back, normal the patient went home. the lab results came back normal, so the patient went home. join two independent clauses with a comma followed by a coordinating conjunction such as so . a comma alone makes a comma splice, and the comma goes before so , not after it.

which revision correctly fixes this sentence? it rained all night, however the orchard did not flood. it rained all night, however, the orchard did not flood. it rained all night however the orchard did not flood. it rained all night; however, the orchard did not flood. it rained all night, and however, the orchard did not flood. however is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction, so it cannot join two sentences with just a comma. use a semicolon before however and a comma after it.

which sentence has parallel structure? before surgery, patients should stop eating, removing jewelry, and the consent form should be signed. before surgery, patients should stop eating, remove jewelry, and sign the consent form. before surgery, patients should stop eating, remove jewelry, and signing the consent form. before surgery, patients should stop eating, jewelry removal, and sign the consent form. items in a list should use the same grammatical form. "stop, remove, sign" are all base-form verbs. the other choices mix verbs with -ing words, nouns or a new clause.

choose the answer that keeps the sentence parallel. the nursing program values honesty, teamwork, and ______. compassion being compassionate to be compassionate they want compassion honesty and teamwork are nouns, so the third item should also be a noun: compassion .

which sentence uses not only ... but also correctly? exercise not only strengthens the heart but also mood improvement. exercise not only strengthens the heart, also improves mood. exercise not only strengthens the heart but also improves mood. not only exercise strengthens the heart but also improves mood. the words after not only and after but also must match: strengthens the heart / improves mood (verb + object). the other choices pair a verb with a noun phrase, drop but , or put not only in front of the wrong word.

which word is a coordinating conjunction? because but although when coordinating conjunctions join equal parts: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so (fanboys). because , although and when are subordinating conjunctions; they begin dependent clauses.
which word is a subordinating conjunction? and or so although although begins a dependent clause (although she was tired, ...). and , or and so are coordinating conjunctions (fanboys).

choose the conjunction that best completes the sentence. the patient took the pain medicine on schedule, ______ her pain did not improve. so because for but the second idea is a surprising contrast to the first, so use the contrast conjunction but . so shows a result, and because and for show a reason; none of these fit the meaning.

which choice combines the two sentences into one complex sentence? the pharmacy was closed. luis drove to the 24-hour pharmacy on shaw avenue. the pharmacy was closed, so luis drove to the 24-hour pharmacy on shaw avenue. the pharmacy was closed; luis drove to the 24-hour pharmacy on shaw avenue. because the pharmacy was closed, luis drove to the 24-hour pharmacy on shaw avenue. the pharmacy was closed, luis drove to the 24-hour pharmacy on shaw avenue. a complex sentence needs a dependent clause. because turns the first sentence into a dependent clause. joining with so or a semicolon makes a

which are complete sentences? select all that apply. wash your hands. after the nurse explained the procedure. the patient, who had been waiting since noon. the doctor smiled. although the clinic was busy, everyone was seen by five. complete: a command with the understood subject you , a simple sentence, and a complex sentence with a main clause. fragments: "after the nurse explained the procedure" is only a dependent clause, and "the patient, who had been waiting since noon" has a subject but no main verb.

which sentences are run-ons or comma splices? select all that apply. the fog was thick on highway 99, drivers slowed down. the fog was thick on highway 99, so drivers slowed down. i studied hard for the teas i still felt nervous. the fog lifted traffic moved faster. the test was hard; i passed it anyway. "the fog was thick on highway 99, drivers slowed down" is a comma splice (two sentences joined by only a comma). "i studied hard for the teas i still felt nervous" and "the fog lifted traffic moved faster" are fused run-ons (no punctuation between the two sentences). "..., so drivers slowed do

in the sentence below, which part is the dependent clause? if you feel dizzy, sit down right away. sit down right away sit down if you feel dizzy you feel dizzy if is a subordinating conjunction, so "if you feel dizzy" cannot stand alone; it is the dependent clause. "sit down right away" is the independent clause (a command). without if , "you feel dizzy" would be independent.

which revision of the sentence has parallel structure? as a medical assistant, i took vital signs, scheduling appointments, and i updated records. as a medical assistant, i took vital signs, scheduled appointments, and updated records. as a medical assistant, i took vital signs, scheduling appointments, and updating records. as a medical assistant, taking vital signs, scheduled appointments, and i updated records. as a medical assistant, i took vital signs, scheduled appointments, and records were updated. all three duties should use the same form: past-tense verbs took , scheduled , updated .

which sentence is most appropriate for an email to the director of a nursing program? hey! when's the deadline for fall?? i am writing to ask about the application deadline for the fall cohort. just wondering when stuff is due for fall lol. yo, i need the fall deadline asap. a message to a program director calls for formal language: complete sentences, no slang, no extra punctuation. the other choices use slang (lol, yo, stuff) and an overly casual or demanding tone.

a student is emailing the nursing director, dr. patel, for the first time. which greeting is most appropriate? dear dr. patel, hey doc, hi there!! what's up, patel, a formal greeting uses the person's title and last name. the other greetings are too casual for a first professional email.

which closing is most appropriate for a professional email to a hiring manager at a hospital? later, ana thx, a sincerely, ana ruiz peace out, ana professional emails close with a formal phrase (sincerely, respectfully, thank you) and your full name. the other closings are slang or abbreviations.

which sentence is best for a printed handout for patients who have no medical background? administer one tablet po q am with meals. ingest the pharmaceutical agent via the oral route daily. just pop a pill whenever you feel like it. take one pill by mouth every morning with food. patient materials should use plain, clear words that anyone can follow. medical abbreviations (po, q am) and overly technical words confuse patients, and "pop a pill whenever" is too casual and gives unsafe directions.
which word has the most formal tone? grab snag score obtain obtain is a formal word meaning "get." grab , snag and score are informal or slang.

a student writes this sentence in a scholarship essay: "nursing school is super hard, but i'm gonna crush it." which revision best fits a formal essay? nursing school is super demanding, but i'm going to crush it. nursing school is demanding, but i am determined to succeed. nursing school is really, really hard, but i will totally do it. nursing school is tough stuff, but i'll nail it. formal writing avoids slang (super, gonna, crush it, nail it), contractions and filler words (really, really; totally). the correct choice keeps the same meaning in a confident, formal tone.

which message best fits a quick text to a close friend? dear friend, i regret to inform you that i shall be delayed by approximately ten minutes. running 10 min late, save me a seat! to whom it may concern: please be advised of my late arrival. per my previous message, my arrival time has been revised. match your language to your audience. a text to a friend can be short and casual. the other choices are so formal that they sound odd in a text to a friend.

a nurse is explaining a procedure to a nervous 7-year-old. which statement is best? the physician will perform an endoscopic examination of your gastrointestinal tract. stop worrying; it's no big deal. the doctor will use a tiny camera to look inside your tummy. i'll be right here with you. you will undergo an upper endoscopy under conscious sedation. for a young child, use simple words and a warm, reassuring tone. technical terms are confusing for a child, and "stop worrying" dismisses the child's feelings.

which sentence best fits a formal lab report? the solution turned an awesome blue super fast! i think the solution kind of turned bluish, maybe. our group was so excited when it turned blue. the solution turned blue after 30 seconds. lab reports use an objective tone: precise, factual and free of opinion or emotion. the other choices add slang, uncertainty or feelings instead of data.

a student cannot attend an interview on tuesday. which sentence is the most professional way to say so in an email? tuesday doesn't work for me, so pick another day. nope, can't do tuesday. unfortunately, i am unavailable on tuesday; would wednesday afternoon work instead? tuesday?? no way. a professional message is polite, explains the problem and offers a solution. the other choices are blunt, demanding or too casual.

a hospital newsletter is announcing a new visitor policy. which sentence has an objective, neutral tone? starting march 1, visitors will be forced to waste time at the front desk. beginning march 1, all visitors must check in at the front desk. the wonderful new policy will make our hospital the safest in california. annoyingly, visitors now have to check in at the front desk. a neutral announcement states the facts without positive or negative opinion words. "forced to waste time" and "annoyingly" are negative, and "wonderful" and "safest" are positive opinions that cannot be proven.

which part of this email sentence should be revised to make it more formal? "i would appreciate it if you could send me the info by friday." i would appreciate it if you could the info by friday info is a casual shortened form; formal writing uses the full word, information . "i would appreciate it if you could" is already polite and formal.

which revision is most appropriate for formal academic writing? "it's important that patients don't skip doses." its important that patients dont skip doses. it's real important that patients don't skip doses. it is important that patients do not skip doses. it is important that patients don't be skipping doses. formal academic writing usually spells out contractions: it is , do not . removing apostrophes creates errors (its, dont), "real important" is informal, and "don't be skipping" is nonstandard.

a respiratory therapist is making a poster for a middle school about vaping. which sentence best fits the audience and purpose? electronic nicotine delivery systems induce pulmonary inflammation via aerosolized particulates. kids who vape are not very smart. vaping has some effects that may or may not matter. vaping can damage your lungs, even if you only do it once in a while. the audience is 11- to 14-year-olds, and the purpose is to warn them. the best sentence is clear, direct and respectful. the technical sentence is too hard for the audience, insulting students will not persuade them, an

which sentence is most appropriate for a formal research paper? several studies suggest that regular exercise lowers blood pressure. you should totally exercise because it lowers your blood pressure. i feel like exercise probably helps blood pressure or whatever. everybody knows exercise lowers blood pressure, duh. research writing is formal and objective and points to evidence ("several studies suggest"). the other choices use slang, speak to "you," or rely on feelings and generalizations.

which word would be least appropriate in a cover letter for a hospital job? dedicated awesome reliable experienced awesome is informal and vague in a professional letter. dedicated , reliable and experienced are professional words that describe job skills.

a student is emailing her chemistry instructor to ask for an extension. which sentences are appropriate for the email? select all that apply. i am writing to request a two-day extension on the lab report. my grandmother was hospitalized this weekend, and i stayed with her. u better say yes, i really need this. thank you for considering my request. whatever you decide is cool, i guess. appropriate: a clear request, a brief and honest reason, and a polite thank-you. inappropriate: text-speak and a demanding tone ("u better say yes") and an informal, careless tone ("cool, i guess").

original sentence: "the kids got sick 'cause the water was nasty." which revisions are written in formal english? select all that apply. the children became ill because the water was contaminated. the kids got sick because the water was gross. the children became sick because the water was unsafe to drink. the children got sick 'cause the water was contaminated. the kiddos became ill since the water was bad. formal revisions replace kids , 'cause and nasty with standard words. the other choices keep at least one informal word: kids, gross, 'cause or kiddos.

which word best describes the tone of this sentence from a clinic flyer? "please remember to fast for eight hours before your blood test; this helps ensure accurate results." informative sarcastic angry humorous the sentence politely gives instructions and explains why, so its tone is informative. there are no jokes, insults or angry words.

which sentence uses respectful, person-first language for a patient's chart? the diabetic in room 3 checks her glucose daily. the sugar patient in room 3 checks her glucose daily. room 3 is a diabetic who checks her glucose daily. the patient in room 3 has diabetes and checks her glucose daily. person-first language names the person first and the condition second: "a patient who has diabetes." the other choices label the person by the condition or by a room number, which health care writing avoids.

which text message from a dental office to its patients is most appropriate? reminder: your cleaning is on tue., may 6, at 2:00 p.m. reply c to confirm. yo ur teeth thing is tues dear valued patient: we hereby formally request the pleasure of your attendance at your forthcoming appointment. don't forget your appointment or else!!! a business text should be short and clear but still professional: date, time and what to do. the other choices are too sloppy, too wordy for a text, or rude.

which revision of this sentence is the most formal? "the doc said i gotta take these meds." the physician said i must take these medications. the doc said i have to take these meds. the physician said i gotta take these medications. the doctor said i gotta take my meds. the formal version replaces every informal word: doc → physician, gotta → must, meds → medications. the other choices still keep at least one informal word.

what is usually the first step of the writing process? editing publishing revising prewriting (brainstorming and planning) writers start by prewriting: brainstorming ideas, researching and planning or outlining. revising, editing and publishing come after a draft exists.

put the steps of the writing process in order from first to last. prewriting drafting revising editing publishing prewriting: brainstorm and plan. drafting: write a first version. revising: improve ideas and organization. editing: fix grammar, spelling and punctuation. publishing: share the final copy.

a student rereads her essay and moves a paragraph so that her ideas flow more logically. which step of the writing process is she doing? editing publishing revising prewriting revising means improving content and organization: adding, deleting, moving or rewording ideas. editing focuses on surface errors such as spelling, punctuation and grammar.

fixing spelling mistakes and comma errors is part of which step of the writing process? revising editing drafting brainstorming editing (also called proofreading) corrects mechanics: spelling, punctuation, capitalization and grammar.

which sentence would make the best thesis statement for an essay arguing that community colleges should offer more nursing seats? nursing is a career that many people choose. california community colleges should expand their nursing programs because hospitals need nurses and many qualified students are turned away. have you ever thought about becoming a nurse? in this essay, i will talk about nursing programs. a strong thesis states a clear, arguable position and previews the main reasons. the other choices are a general fact, a question and an announcement; none of them takes a position.

choose the best topic sentence for this paragraph. ______ almonds supply vitamin e and magnesium. they also contain fiber, which helps digestion. a small handful has about 6 grams of protein. almonds are a nutritious snack. california grows most of the world's almonds. some people are allergic to tree nuts. almond trees bloom in february. every supporting sentence describes a nutritional benefit, so the topic sentence should introduce almonds' nutrition. the other choices are true but are about farming or allergies, not the paragraph's main idea.

which sentence does not belong in this paragraph? (1) valley fever is caused by a fungus that lives in the soil of the southern san joaquin valley. (2) when dust is stirred up, people can breathe in the fungal spores. (3) fresno state has a well-known agriculture program. (4) most people who are infected have mild, flu-like symptoms or none at all. sentence 1 sentence 2 sentence 3 sentence 4 the paragraph is about valley fever: its cause, how it spreads and its symptoms. sentence 3 is about a university program and does not support the main idea.

choose the transition that best completes the passage. regular exercise lowers blood pressure. ______, people who exercise too hard without warming up may get injured. therefore for example similarly however the second sentence presents a contrast (a possible downside), so a contrast transition such as however fits. therefore shows a result, for example gives an example and similarly shows likeness.

choose the transition that best completes the passage. the heat index reached 110 °f. ______, fresno county opened cooling centers. as a result however for instance in contrast opening cooling centers was caused by the heat, so a cause-and-effect transition fits: as a result .

choose the transition that best completes the passage. many foods are high in potassium. ______, one medium banana has about 420 mg. nevertheless in conclusion for example meanwhile the second sentence gives a specific example of a high-potassium food, so for example fits.

choose the transition that best completes these instructions. first, wash your hands for at least 20 seconds. ______, put on a clean pair of gloves. next however in contrast for example the instructions describe steps in time order, so a sequence word such as next fits. the other choices signal contrast or an example, which does not match a list of steps.

put these sentences in the most logical order to form a paragraph. hand hygiene is the most important way to prevent infections in hospitals. germs can travel from one patient to another on a health care worker's hands. for this reason, staff wash or sanitize their hands before and after every patient contact. following this simple step prevents many infections every day. start with the topic sentence (the main idea). next comes the explanation (how germs spread), then "for this reason" (the response), and last the concluding sentence.

put these sentences in chronological order to form a paragraph. elena first became interested in health care while volunteering at a fresno clinic in high school. after graduation, she enrolled at a community college and took chemistry and anatomy. two years later, she passed the teas and was accepted into a nursing program. today, she works as a registered nurse at the same clinic where she once volunteered. time words show the order: "in high school" → "after graduation" → "two years later" → "today."

which situation is plagiarism? copying two sentences from a website into your essay without quotation marks or a citation quoting a sentence from a journal article and citing the article summarizing a textbook chapter in your own words and citing the textbook stating that the heart pumps blood without citing a source plagiarism is presenting someone else's words or ideas as your own. copying without quotation marks or a citation is plagiarism. common knowledge, such as the fact that the heart pumps blood, does not need a citation.

a student rewrites an idea from a journal article completely in her own words. what should she do? nothing, because she used her own words. put the paraphrase in quotation marks. cite the article, because the idea came from it. remove the idea, because paraphrasing is not allowed. a paraphrase uses your own words, but the idea still belongs to the original author, so it must be cited. quotation marks are only for an author's exact words.

which source would be most credible for a research paper on childhood vaccine safety? a social media post from a parenting group a report from the centers for disease control and prevention an anonymous personal blog an advertisement from a supplement company credible sources come from experts or trusted organizations, are reviewed, and have no reason to sell you something. social media posts, anonymous blogs and ads are not reliable for research.

which sentence is the best concluding sentence for a paragraph about the benefits of sleep for college students? some animals sleep during the day. next, i will explain how caffeine affects the brain. getting enough sleep is one of the simplest ways students can improve their health and their grades. many dorm rooms have small beds. a concluding sentence sums up the paragraph's main idea. the other choices are off topic or introduce a new subject.

where is the best place to add this sentence to the paragraph? for example, a 12-ounce can of soda contains about 39 grams of sugar. (1) sugary drinks are a major source of added sugar. (2) choosing water instead can lower the risk of type 2 diabetes. (3) unsweetened tea and sparkling water are other good choices. before sentence 1 after sentence 1 after sentence 2 after sentence 3 an example should come right after the claim it supports. the soda example supports sentence 1 (sugary drinks contain a lot of added sugar). sentences 2 and 3 are about healthier choices.

which tasks are part of revising (not editing or publishing)? select all that apply. adding details to support a weak point correcting a misspelled word moving paragraphs so the ideas flow better deleting a sentence that is off topic choosing a font for the final copy revising changes the content and organization: adding support, reordering ideas, cutting off-topic sentences. fixing spelling is editing, and choosing a font for the final copy is part of publishing.

which of the following need a citation in a research paper? select all that apply. a direct quotation from a nursing journal a statistic from a cdc report a paraphrase of a textbook author's argument the fact that the human heart has four chambers your own opinion about the topic cite quotations, statistics and paraphrased ideas, because they come from someone else. common knowledge (the heart has four chambers) and your own opinions do not need a citation.

what is the main purpose of an outline? to check the final copy for spelling errors to list the sources at the end of the paper to share the finished paper with readers to organize main ideas and supporting details before drafting an outline is a prewriting tool that arranges the main points and their support in a logical order. spell-checking is editing, a source list is a works-cited or reference page, and sharing the paper is publishing.

paragraph 1 of an essay describes the benefits of telehealth. paragraph 2 describes its drawbacks. which sentence is the best way to begin paragraph 2? in addition to these advantages, telehealth has even more benefits. despite these advantages, telehealth also has limitations. as a result, telehealth is the perfect solution for every patient. for example, telehealth saves patients travel time. paragraph 2 shifts from benefits to drawbacks, so it needs a contrast transition that links back to paragraph 1. the other choices continue the list of benefits or draw a conclusion the paragraph does n

what does the prefix hyper- mean, as in hypertension ? below normal; deficient slow around above normal; excessive hyper- means above normal or excessive. hypertension = high blood pressure. hypo- means below normal, brady- means slow and peri- means around.

using word parts, what does hypoglycemia mean? ( glyc- = sugar; -emia = blood condition) high blood sugar low blood sugar sugar in the urine a fast heart rate hypo- (below normal) + glyc (sugar) + -emia (blood condition) = low blood sugar. high blood sugar would be hyper glycemia.

what does dermatitis mean? surgical removal of skin the study of the skin pain in the skin inflammation of the skin dermat- means skin and -itis means inflammation. removal would be -ectomy , study would be -ology and pain would be -algia .

what does appendectomy mean? inflammation of the appendix surgical removal of the appendix a surgical incision into the appendix an x-ray image of the appendix -ectomy means surgical removal (cutting out). inflammation is -itis (appendicitis), a surgical incision is -otomy and an x-ray image would be -gram or -graphy .
the root cardi- (as in cardiology ) refers to the: heart lungs kidneys liver cardi- means heart. the lungs are pulmon- or pneum- , the kidneys are nephr- or ren- , and the liver is hepat- .

an adult patient's heart rate is 45 beats per minute, which is slower than normal. which term describes this? bradycardia tachycardia cardiomegaly hypertension brady- means slow and cardi means heart: bradycardia = slow heart rate. tachy- means fast, cardiomegaly is an enlarged heart and hypertension is high blood pressure.

the root arthr- means joint. what does arthralgia mean? joint inflammation joint pain surgical removal of a joint fusion of a joint -algia means pain, so arthralgia = joint pain. joint inflammation is arthritis (-itis).
a nephrologist is a doctor who specializes in the: nerves liver kidneys heart nephr- means kidney and -ologist means specialist. do not confuse nephr- (kidney) with neur- (nerve).

what does hepatitis mean? inflammation of the liver inflammation of the kidney inflammation of the stomach inflammation of the skin hepat- means liver and -itis means inflammation. kidney inflammation is nephritis, stomach inflammation is gastritis and skin inflammation is dermatitis.

using word parts, what does tachypnea most likely mean? ( -pnea = breathing) slow breathing absence of breathing rapid breathing painful breathing tachy- means fast and -pnea means breathing, so tachypnea = rapid breathing. slow breathing is bradypnea, and absence of breathing is apnea ( a- = without).

what does the prefix in antibacterial mean? before between against without anti- means against: antibacterial = working against bacteria. before is pre- or ante- , between is inter- and without is a- or an- .
a neurologist is a specialist in the: kidneys blood skin nervous system neur- means nerve, and -ologist means one who studies or specializes. kidneys = nephr-, blood = hem- or hemat-, skin = derm-.

read the sentence and use context clues. the cut was so superficial that it affected only the top layer of skin and did not need stitches. what does superficial most nearly mean? very deep on the surface infected painful the clue "affected only the top layer of skin" tells you the cut stayed on the surface. a deep cut would usually need stitches, so "very deep" contradicts the sentence.

the usually taciturn patient surprised the nurses by chatting for an hour about his grandchildren. based on the context, what does taciturn most nearly mean? quiet and reserved cheerful and friendly confused and forgetful angry and impatient the word "surprised" signals a contrast: chatting for an hour was unusual for him. so taciturn must mean the opposite of talkative: quiet and reserved. cheerful, confused and angry don't create the contrast with chatting that the sentence sets up.

read the sentence and use context clues. the patient was lethargic ; he slept most of the day and barely responded when spoken to. what does lethargic most nearly mean? excited and restless in severe pain very hungry sluggish and drowsy the semicolon introduces an explanation: sleeping most of the day and barely responding describe someone sluggish and drowsy. nothing in the sentence mentions pain, hunger or restlessness.

read the sentence and use context clues. the nurse tried to alleviate the patient's anxiety by explaining each step of the procedure and holding her hand. what does alleviate most nearly mean? increase ignore measure relieve explaining each step and holding her hand are comforting actions, so the nurse is trying to reduce, or relieve, the anxiety. a nurse would not try to increase or ignore anxiety with comforting actions.

read the sentences and use context clues. the new medication proved highly efficacious . the patient's symptoms disappeared within two days, and the doctor began prescribing it to other patients. what does efficacious most nearly mean? expensive dangerous effective experimental the symptoms disappeared and the doctor wanted to use it again, so the medicine worked well. nothing in the sentences mentions cost or danger, and a medicine that has "proved" itself is no longer just experimental.

the prefix peri- means "around." what is the pericardium ? the sac that surrounds the heart the inner lining of the heart a single heart muscle cell a blood vessel leaving the heart peri- (around) + cardi (heart) = the membrane sac around the heart. the inner lining of the heart is the endocardium ( endo- = within).
type the suffix that means "surgical removal," as in tonsillectomy and mastectomy . (you do not need to type the hyphen.) -ectomy means surgical removal. tonsill + ectomy = removal of the tonsils.

type the root that means "skin," as in dermatitis and epidermis . (you do not need to type the hyphen.) derm- (also written derma- or dermat- ) means skin. the epidermis is the outer layer of skin ( epi- = upon).

which terms describe a condition that is below normal? select all that apply. hypothermia hypotension hyperglycemia hypokalemia tachycardia hypo- means below normal: low body temperature (hypothermia), low blood pressure (hypotension) and low blood potassium (hypokalemia). hyper glycemia is high blood sugar, and tachy cardia is a fast heart rate.

which words contain a prefix meaning "not" or "without"? select all that apply. atypical unconscious preoperative nonsterile postpartum a- (without), un- (not) and non- (not) are negative prefixes: atypical, unconscious, nonsterile. pre- means before and post- means after.

which phrase is redundant (says the same thing twice)? past history medical history recent visit daily dose history is always in the past, so "past history" repeats itself. the other phrases each add new information.

which revision is most concise? "due to the fact that the clinic was closed, we went to urgent care." because the clinic was closed, we went to urgent care. due to the fact of the clinic being closed, we went to urgent care. in light of the fact that the clinic was closed, we went to urgent care. owing to the fact that the clinic was closed, we went to urgent care. "due to the fact that" is a wordy way to say because . the other choices just swap in different wordy phrases.

which sentence has no redundant words? the nurse repeated the instructions again. the nurse repeated the instructions over again. the nurse repeated the instructions. the nurse repeated and restated the instructions again. repeat already means "say again," so adding again or over again is redundant.

which revision is the most concise? "at this point in time, the doctor is with another patient." at this point in time, the doctor is currently with another patient. the doctor is with another patient now. at this present time, the doctor is with another patient. at the current point in time, the doctor is now with another patient. "at this point in time" means now . the other choices keep the wordy phrase or add more repetition (currently, now).

which sentence is clear, with no ambiguous pronoun? ana told maria that she needed to update the chart. when ana called maria, she was at the pharmacy. ana and maria met before she left for her shift. ana told maria, “i need to update the chart.” in the other choices, she could mean ana or maria. quoting ana's words makes it clear that ana is the one who needs to update the chart.

which revision makes this sentence clear? "the nurse put the medication on the tray and then cleaned it." the nurse put the medication on the tray and then cleaned it off. the nurse put the medication on the tray and then cleaned the tray. the nurse put the medication on the tray and then cleaned it thoroughly. the nurse put the medication on the tray, and then it was cleaned. in the original, it could mean the medication or the tray. replacing it with the noun ( the tray ) removes the confusion. the other choices still use the unclear it .

choose the most precise word to complete the sentence. the patient's temperature ______ from 98.6 °f to 103 °f in two hours. rose changed went happened rose tells the reader exactly which way the temperature moved: up. changed and went are vague, and happened does not make sense.

which instruction is the most precise? take some tablets every so often. take a couple of tablets a few times a day. take 2 tablets every 6 hours with water. take the tablets regularly. precise writing gives exact numbers and times: 2 tablets, every 6 hours. vague words such as some , a couple , a few and regularly could lead to a dosing error.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the clinic saw ______ patients this week than last week. less lesser littler fewer use fewer for things you can count (patients) and less for amounts you measure (less water, less time).

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. from the doctor's smile, the patient ______ that the news was good. inferred implied implicated inflected to infer is to draw a conclusion from clues; the listener infers. to imply is to hint; the speaker implies. here the patient is drawing the conclusion.

choose the word that correctly completes the sentence. the clinic accepts all insurance plans ______ one. accept expect excess except except means "other than" or "leaving out." accept means to receive, expect means to anticipate and excess means too much.

which is the most concise version of this sentence? "the reason why she was late is because the bus was delayed." she was late because the bus was delayed. the reason why she was late is that the bus was delayed. the reason she was late is due to the fact that the bus was delayed. the reason why is because she was late since the bus was delayed. "the reason why ... is because" says the same thing three times (reason, why, because). start with the subject and verb, then give the cause: "she was late because ..."

which single word best replaces very tired to make this sentence more precise? after a 12-hour night shift, the nurse was very tired. sleepy drowsy exhausted bored exhausted means extremely tired, so it replaces both words with one strong word. sleepy and drowsy mean wanting to sleep, not extreme tiredness, and bored means something else.

which sentence is free of redundancy? each patient received a free gift. each patient received a sample of lotion. the final outcome of the study was positive. the nurses will meet together at 3 p.m. a gift is already free, an outcome is already final, and meet already means come together. "a sample of lotion" has no repeated meaning.

which sentence is the clearest and most direct? the medication was given to the patient at noon by the nurse. at noon, there was the giving of medication by the nurse to the patient. the nurse gave the patient her medication at noon. it was at noon that the medication was what the nurse gave to the patient. active voice (subject → action → receiver) is usually the clearest: "the nurse gave ..." the passive version is grammatical but wordier, and the last two choices are awkward and hard to follow.

which revision removes the wordiness from this sentence? "in order to apply, you need to fill out the form in its entirety." in order to apply, you need to complete the form in its entirety. to apply, complete the entire form. to apply, you need to fill out the form in its entirety completely. in order for you to apply, fill out the entire whole form. "in order to" can be shortened to to , and "fill out ... in its entirety" can be shortened to complete the entire form . the other choices keep the wordy phrases or add redundancy (entirety completely, entire whole).

which phrases are redundant? select all that apply. end result advance planning free gift blood test annual checkup a result comes at the end, planning is done in advance, and a gift is free, so these phrases repeat themselves. "blood test" and "annual checkup" each add information.

which sentences contain an ambiguous pronoun? select all that apply. when the doctor spoke with the patient, he seemed worried. carlos called his mother after his shift ended. take the cap off the bottle and throw it away. the nurses told the students that they would be late. the pharmacist checked the label before she filled the prescription. ambiguous: he (doctor or patient?), it (cap or bottle?) and they (nurses or students?). clear: carlos is the only person who can own the mother and the shift, and the pharmacist is the only person in the last sentence.

which word has the most positive connotation for describing a patient who asks many questions about her care? nosy demanding engaged pushy engaged suggests the patient is interested and involved in her care, which is positive. nosy , demanding and pushy all have negative connotations.

which choice combines these sentences most concisely? the clinic is in merced. the clinic offers free flu shots. the flu shots are offered on saturdays. the clinic is in merced, and the clinic offers free flu shots, and they are on saturdays. in merced is the clinic, which offers flu shots that are free and that are on saturdays. the clinic, which is in merced, offers flu shots, which are free, which are on saturdays. the clinic in merced offers free flu shots on saturdays. combine the details into one subject and one verb: "the clinic in merced offers free flu shots on saturdays." the other c

which revision replaces the vague word stuff with precise language? "bring your stuff to the appointment." bring your things to the appointment. bring all your stuff and things to the appointment. bring whatever you need to the appointment. bring your insurance card and medication list to the appointment. precise language names exactly what to bring. things and whatever you need are as vague as stuff .

which sentence uses standard english word choice? irregardless of the heat, the clinic stayed open. regardless of the heat, the clinic stayed open. the heat could of caused her dizziness. she was laying on the couch all afternoon. regardless is standard; "irregardless" is nonstandard (the ir- and -less both mean "not"). "could of" should be could have , and a person reclining is lying , not "laying."

which decimal is equal to 3/8? 0.125 0.375 0.0375 2.667 a fraction bar means divide: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. 2.667 comes from dividing the wrong way (8 ÷ 3). 0.0375 has the decimal point one place too far left, and 0.125 is only 1/8, not 3/8.

a patient's chart says 0.45 of the meal tray was eaten. what is 0.45 written as a percent? 45% 450% 0.45% 4.5% to change a decimal to a percent, multiply by 100 (move the decimal point 2 places right). 0.45 × 100 = 45, so 0.45 = 45%. 4.5% and 450% move the decimal the wrong number of places; 0.45% does not move it at all.
write 72% as a decimal. percent means "per hundred," so divide by 100. 72 ÷ 100 = 0.72 (move the decimal point 2 places left).

which improper fraction is equal to 2 1/4? 8/4 3/4 6/4 9/4 multiply the whole number by the denominator, then add the numerator: 2 × 4 + 1 = 9. keep the same denominator: 2 1/4 = 9/4. 8/4 forgets to add the 1, and 6/4 multiplies 2 × 1 before adding 4.

which of these values is the greatest? 0.6 5/8 0.615 62% change everything to decimals: 5/8 = 0.625, 62% = 0.62, 0.6 = 0.600, 0.615 = 0.615. compare place by place: 0.625 > 0.620 > 0.615 > 0.600. 62% looks big because 62 is a large number, but as a decimal it is 0.62, which is less than 0.625.

which values are equivalent to 3/5? select all that apply. 0.6 0.35 60% 9/15 5/3 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6, and 0.6 × 100 = 60%. 9/15 simplifies to 3/5 when you divide the top and bottom by 3. 0.35 just writes the digits 3 and 5 after a decimal point, and 5/3 flips the fraction (it is about 1.67).

put these numbers in order from least to greatest. 0.09 1/8 0.2 23% 1/4 convert to decimals: 0.09, 1/8 = 0.125, 0.2 = 0.20, 23% = 0.23, 1/4 = 0.25. line up the decimal places: 0.090 < 0.125 < 0.200 < 0.230 < 0.250. watch out for 0.09: it is less than 0.2 even though 9 is bigger than 2, because 0.09 means 9 hundredths.

a patient finished 2/3 of a bottle of a nutrition shake. about what percent of the shake did the patient drink? round to the nearest whole percent. 150% 66% 67% 23% 2 ÷ 3 = 0.6666…, and 0.6666… × 100 = 66.66…%. the digit after the 6 in the ones place is 6, so round up: about 67%. 66% chops off the decimals instead of rounding, 23% just writes the digits 2 and 3, and 150% comes from 3 ÷ 2.
write 0.875 as a fraction in lowest terms. (type it like 3/4.) 0.875 is 875 thousandths: 875/1000. divide the top and bottom by 125: 875 ÷ 125 = 7 and 1000 ÷ 125 = 8. so 0.875 = 7/8.

a medicated cream is 1.5% hydrocortisone. what is 1.5% written as a decimal? 0.015 0.0015 0.15 1.5 divide by 100: move the decimal point 2 places to the left. 1.5 → 0.15 → 0.015. 0.15 moves only one place, and 0.0015 moves three places.

which fraction is between 1/2 and 3/4? 5/8 7/8 4/5 3/8 write all of them in eighths or as decimals: 1/2 = 0.5 and 3/4 = 0.75. 5/8 = 0.625, which is between 0.5 and 0.75. 3/8 = 0.375 is too small; 7/8 = 0.875 and 4/5 = 0.8 are too large.

which list shows the numbers in order from least to greatest ? 0.7, 7/9, 72%, 3/4 72%, 0.7, 7/9, 3/4 0.7, 72%, 3/4, 7/9 7/9, 3/4, 72%, 0.7 convert: 0.7 = 0.700, 72% = 0.720, 3/4 = 0.750, 7/9 ≈ 0.778. least to greatest: 0.700, 0.720, 0.750, 0.778. the list starting with 7/9 is greatest to least (backwards). putting 7/9 second treats it as smaller than it is: 7 ÷ 9 ≈ 0.778.
which fraction is equal to 0.3? 1/3 3/100 30/10 3/10 0.3 means 3 tenths, so it is 3/10. 1/3 is 0.333…, which is close but not equal. 3/100 is 0.03, and 30/10 is 3.

an almond grower in madera county has harvested 18 of the 24 rows in an orchard. what percent of the rows have been harvested? 75% 18% 25% 133% percent harvested = part ÷ whole × 100 = 18 ÷ 24 × 100. 18 ÷ 24 = 0.75, and 0.75 × 100 = 75%. 25% is the percent not harvested. 133% comes from dividing 24 ÷ 18 (whole ÷ part).

write 5/12 as a decimal rounded to the nearest hundredth. 4.17 0.42 0.41 2.40 5 ÷ 12 = 0.41666… to round to the hundredths place, look at the thousandths digit: it is 6, so round the 1 up to 2. the answer is 0.42. 0.41 truncates instead of rounding, 2.40 is 12 ÷ 5, and 4.17 has the decimal point in the wrong place.

what is 3/20 written as a percent? 1.5% 0.15% 60% 15% make the denominator 100: multiply top and bottom by 5 → 3/20 = 15/100. 15/100 = 15%. 0.15% and 1.5% misplace the decimal, and 60% multiplies 3 × 20 instead of dividing.

a nurse sets a fluid goal of 2 1/2 liters for a patient. by noon the patient has had 1.75 l. what percent of the goal has the patient reached? change the mixed number to a decimal: 2 1/2 = 2.5 l. part ÷ whole = 1.75 ÷ 2.5 = 0.7. 0.7 × 100 = 70%.

which decimal is equal to 7/25? 3.57 0.07 0.725 0.28 multiply the top and bottom by 4 to get a denominator of 100: 7/25 = 28/100. 28/100 = 0.28. 3.57 is 25 ÷ 7 (upside down), 0.725 just strings the digits together, and 0.07 ignores the 25.
write 0.6 as a percent. multiply by 100: 0.6 × 100 = 60. so 0.6 = 60%. (it is not 6%; 0.6 means 6 tenths, which is 60 hundredths.)

which values are greater than 2/3? select all that apply. 0.7 0.66 69% 13/20 5/7 2/3 = 0.666…, so compare each value to 0.667. 0.7, 69% = 0.69, and 5/7 ≈ 0.714 are all greater. 0.66 is a trap: 0.660 is less than 0.666…. 13/20 = 0.65 is also less.

which mixed number is equal to 11/4? 2 1/4 3 3/4 2 3/4 3 1/4 divide: 11 ÷ 4 = 2 with a remainder of 3. the remainder becomes the new numerator: 11/4 = 2 3/4. check: 2 × 4 + 3 = 11. the other choices give 9/4, 13/4, and 15/4.

evaluate: 8 + 4 × 3 20 36 96 15 multiplication comes before addition: 4 × 3 = 12. then add: 8 + 12 = 20. 36 works left to right ((8 + 4) × 3), which ignores the order of operations. 15 adds all three numbers, and 96 multiplies all three.

evaluate: 18 − 6 ÷ 3 + 2² 8 12 20 16 exponent first: 2² = 4. then divide: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. finally add and subtract left to right: 18 − 2 + 4 = 20. 8 comes from doing 18 − 6 first. 12 subtracts the 4 instead of adding it, and 16 forgets the + 4.
what is −7 + 12? −5 5 19 −19 the signs are different, so subtract the absolute values: 12 − 7 = 5. keep the sign of the number with the larger absolute value (12 is positive), so the answer is 5.
what is (−6)(−4)? 24 −10 −24 10 a negative times a negative is positive. 6 × 4 = 24, so (−6)(−4) = 24. −10 and 10 add the numbers instead of multiplying.
evaluate: −15 ÷ 3 − (−4) divide first: −15 ÷ 3 = −5. subtracting a negative is the same as adding: −5 − (−4) = −5 + 4. −5 + 4 = −1.

what is 3/4 + 2/3? 1 5/12 5/7 1 1/8 1/2 use a common denominator of 12: 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12. 9/12 + 8/12 = 17/12 = 1 5/12. 5/7 adds the tops and the bottoms, which is never allowed. 1/2 multiplies the fractions, and 1 1/8 (9/8) divides them.

what is 2 1/2 × 1 1/3? 1 7/8 2 1/6 3 5/6 3 1/3 change to improper fractions: 2 1/2 = 5/2 and 1 1/3 = 4/3. multiply: 5/2 × 4/3 = 20/6 = 10/3 = 3 1/3. 2 1/6 multiplies the whole numbers and the fractions separately. 3 5/6 adds instead of multiplying, and 1 7/8 divides.

a patient's temperature is recorded as 99.368°f on a digital readout. what is this rounded to the nearest tenth? 99.4°f 99.37°f 99°f 99.3°f the tenths digit is 3. look at the digit to its right (the hundredths digit): 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round the 3 up to 4: 99.4°f. 99.37 rounds to the hundredth, and 99 rounds to the whole number.
round 0.04682 to the nearest hundredth. the hundredths digit is 4 (0.0 4 682). the next digit is 6, so round up: 0.04 → 0.05.

a bottle holds 4.2 oz of infant formula, and the baby drinks 1.75 oz. how much formula is left in the bottle? 3.45 oz 2.45 oz 5.95 oz 3.55 oz line up the decimal points and write 4.2 as 4.20. 4.20 − 1.75 = 2.45 oz. 3.55 subtracts the smaller digit from the larger in each place instead of borrowing, 3.45 subtracts only 0.75, and 5.95 adds instead of subtracting.

what is 0.6 × 0.04? 2.4 0.24 0.024 0.0024 multiply as whole numbers: 6 × 4 = 24. count the decimal places in the factors: 0.6 has 1 and 0.04 has 2, for a total of 3. put 3 decimal places in the answer: 0.024.
what is 3.6 ÷ 0.09? move both decimal points 2 places right so you divide by a whole number: 3.6 ÷ 0.09 = 360 ÷ 9. 360 ÷ 9 = 40. check: 40 × 0.09 = 3.6 ✓

evaluate: −2(5 − 9)² ÷ 4 + 3 11 −11 19 −5 parentheses: 5 − 9 = −4. exponent: (−4)² = 16 (a negative squared is positive). multiply and divide left to right: −2 × 16 = −32, then −32 ÷ 4 = −8. add: −8 + 3 = −5. choice 11 treats (−4)² as −16; 19 squares the −2 as well; −11 subtracts the 3.

which expressions are equal to −12? select all that apply. (−3)(4) −24 ÷ (−2) −20 + 8 −4 − (−8) 6 − 18 (−3)(4) = −12, −20 + 8 = −12, and 6 − 18 = −12. −24 ÷ (−2) = +12, because a negative divided by a negative is positive. −4 − (−8) = −4 + 8 = 4.
evaluate: 15 − 3 × 4 multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12. then subtract: 15 − 12 = 3. (working left to right would give 48, which is wrong.)

early on a winter morning near huntington lake in the sierra, the temperature was −6°f. by afternoon it had risen 23 degrees. what was the afternoon temperature? 29°f −29°f 17°f −17°f "risen" means add: −6 + 23. different signs: 23 − 6 = 17, and the larger number (23) is positive, so the answer is 17°f. −29 subtracts instead of adding, and 29 ignores the negative sign on −6.

evaluate (3/4 − 1/3) ÷ 5/8. write your answer as a fraction in lowest terms. parentheses first, with a denominator of 12: 9/12 − 4/12 = 5/12. to divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal: 5/12 × 8/5. 5/12 × 8/5 = 40/60 = 2/3.

a clinic's supply budget spreadsheet shows a cost of $18.4562 per box of gloves. what is this rounded to the nearest cent? $18.456 $18.46 $18.45 $18.50 the nearest cent is the hundredths place: $18.4 5 62. the next digit is 6, so round the 5 up: $18.46. $18.45 truncates, $18.50 rounds to the nearest dime, and $18.456 rounds to the thousandth.

which numbers are less than −1? select all that apply. −1.5 −0.9 −5/4 −1 −2.01 on a number line, "less than −1" means to the left of −1. −1.5, −5/4 (= −1.25), and −2.01 are all left of −1. −0.9 is to the right of −1 (closer to zero), and −1 is equal to −1, not less than it.

a student in merced has $45.20 in a checking account. she pays two bills of $62.75 and $18.30, then deposits $40.00. what is her balance now? −$4.15 −$35.85 $22.45 $4.15 write it as one expression: 45.20 − 62.75 − 18.30 + 40.00. 45.20 − 62.75 = −17.55; −17.55 − 18.30 = −35.85; −35.85 + 40.00 = 4.15. −$35.85 forgets the deposit, and $22.45 forgets the second bill.

put these numbers in order from least to greatest. −2.5 −1 3/4 −1.2 0.4 3/2 convert: −1 3/4 = −1.75 and 3/2 = 1.5. the most negative number is the least: −2.5 < −1.75 < −1.2. then the positives: 0.4 < 1.5.

a recipe needs 1/2 cup of oil per batch. how many batches can be made with 6.5 cups of oil? 7 13 6 3.25 number of batches = 6.5 ÷ 1/2. dividing by 1/2 is the same as multiplying by 2: 6.5 × 2 = 13. 3.25 multiplies by 1/2 instead of dividing.

on a night shift, a hospital unit has 4 nurses for 28 patients. what is the ratio of nurses to patients in simplest form? 4:7 1:24 1:7 7:1 write nurses first: 4:28. divide both parts by 4: 4 ÷ 4 = 1 and 28 ÷ 4 = 7, so the ratio is 1:7. 7:1 reverses the order (patients to nurses). 1:24 subtracts instead of dividing.

a recipe uses 3 cups of flour to make 2 dozen tortillas. how many cups of flour are needed for 5 dozen tortillas? 3.33 7.5 6 15 set up a proportion: 3 cups / 2 dozen = x cups / 5 dozen. cross-multiply: 2x = 3 × 5 = 15, so x = 7.5 cups. 3.33 flips the ratio (2/3 × 5). 6 adds 3 extra cups for 3 extra dozen instead of scaling, and 15 forgets to divide by 2.
solve the proportion: x/12 = 15/36 cross-multiply: 36x = 12 × 15 = 180. divide: x = 180 ÷ 36 = 5. or notice 15/36 = 5/12, so x = 5.

a drive from fresno to bakersfield covers 110 miles and takes 1 hour 50 minutes. what is the average speed in miles per hour? 55 mph 73.3 mph 60 mph 1 mph change the time to hours: 50 minutes = 50/60 = 5/6 hour, so 1 hour 50 min = 1 5/6 = 11/6 hours. speed = distance ÷ time = 110 ÷ 11/6 = 110 × 6/11 = 60 mph. 73.3 mph treats 1 hr 50 min as 1.5 hours. 55 mph rounds the time up to 2 hours, and 1 is miles per minute (110 mi ÷ 110 min).
